question.latex:
A non-volatile, non-electrolyte solid solute when dissolved in $40$ g of a solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreased from $760$ mm Hg to $750$ mm Hg. If the same solution boils at $320$ K, then the number of moles of the solvent present in the solution is \_\_\_\_\_. $Nearest integer$
[Given: boiling point of the pure solvent $= 319.5$ K, $K_b$ of the solvent $= 0.3$ K kg mol$^{-1}$]
question.unicode:
A non-volatile, non-electrolyte solid solute when dissolved in 40 g of a solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreased from 760 mm Hg to 750 mm Hg. If the same solution boils at 320 K, then the number of moles of the solvent present in the solution is _____. Nearest integer
[Given: boiling point of the pure solvent = 319.5 K, K_b of the solvent = 0.3 K kg mol^{-1}]
question.plainText: A non-volatile, non-electrolyte solid solute when dissolved in 40 g of a solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreased from 760 mm Hg to 750 mm Hg. If the same solution boils at 320 K, then the number of moles of the solvent present in the solution is _____. Nearest integer [Given: boiling point of the pure solvent = 319.5 K, K_b of the solvent = 0.3 K kg mol^{-1}]

explanation.latex:
Applying Raoult's law for lowering of vapor pressure:
$\frac{P^\circ - P_s}{P^\circ} = x_{\text{solute}} \implies \frac{760 - 750}{760} = \frac{10}{760} = \frac{1}{76}$.
Let $n$ be the moles of the solute and $N$ be the moles of the solvent.
Mole fraction of solute, $x_{\text{solute}} = \frac{n}{n + N} = \frac{1}{76}$.
$n + N = 76n \implies N = 75n$.
The elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^\circ = 320 - 319.5 = 0.5$ K.
$\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$, where molality $m = \frac{\text{Moles of solute } (n)}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}} = \frac{n}{0.040}$.
$0.5 = 0.3 \times \frac{n}{0.040}$.
Solving for $n$: $n = \frac{0.5 \times 0.040}{0.3} = \frac{0.020}{0.3} = \frac{1}{15}$ moles.
Using the relationship derived from mole fraction: $N = 75n = 75 \times \left(\frac{1}{15}\right) = 5$ moles.
